what: Three screens drawn as the conventions say since ADR-003: native frames named 'S01 — Sign in', 'S02 — Dashboard' and 'S03 — Settings', each with the matching element id, every member carrying frameId. S01 and S03 hold no heading; S02 holds a 26px heading of its own, 'Welcome back'. Two bound arrows run from a button to the next frame. Then, in a real tab, a note 'Move this to a header bar' under S02's 'Sign out', and S02 renamed 'S02 — Home'.
why: The fixture ADR-003's 'Enforced by' asks for. Each screen must be named by its frame, not by a heading (S02's heading is listed as a component, and does not name the screen); a bound arrow to a frame must be navigation to that screen, after a tab has loaded and synced it; a frame a person renamed is still a screen, named by the new name, not markup; a note inside a frame binds to the component it sits by.

markup.text: Move this to a header bar

notes: Drawn through the CLI on a canvas on port 3071 with a tab open, 2026-11-16; the note and the rename were made in that tab (by an agent driving the browser pane, so origin 'human' is the tab's, not a person's), then the scene was exported. Before the reading knew frames, the same frames read S01 and S03 unnamed and S02 as 'Welcome back'.

Before the page bound arrows to frames (SPEC-005, finding 1), the tab's first sync reported flow-1 and flow-2 as edited by a human, end binding dropped, and the reading listed both as markup instead of navigation.
S02 reads 'drawn by human' because its last edit, the rename, came from the tab; the reading marks any element a person last wrote that way.
The 2 inferred are s02-card (card?) and s03-dark (checkbox?, with 'Dark mode' folded in).
